claims.text: The baseline MnNiSi₀.₆₂(FeCoGe)₀.₃₈ alloy has a compressive strength of approximately 50 MPa.
The baseline alloy has poor mechanical integrity.
A 10 vol% interconnected Cu phase can be introduced by molten-Cu infiltration of a sintered porous HEA preform.
The infiltrated Cu will form a ductile network that bridges HEA grains and toughens grain boundaries.
The Cu network will redistribute stress and provide plastic accommodation.
Stress redistribution and plastic accommodation by Cu will arrest crack initiation and propagation.
The Cu-containing composite will reach a compressive strength of at least 300 MPa.
Copper's high thermal conductivity will preserve rapid heat flow in the composite.
Preserving rapid heat flow will leave the martensitic/ferromagnetic transition effectively unchanged.
A martensitic/ferromagnetic transition is responsible for the alloy's caloric effect.
The 10 vol% Cu composite will retain at least 90% of the baseline adiabatic temperature change under a 2 T magnetic field at the transformation temperature.
The proposed strength and caloric-retention behavior is valid at 290–310 K, at 2 T, under quasi-static loading at strain rates no greater than 10⁻³ s⁻¹, and for approximately 10 ± 2 vol% Cu.
The resulting strength or caloric retention may vary by approximately ±10%.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts compressive strength of at least 300 MPa, but the stated experiment only falsifies it below 250 MPa. Results from 250 to below 300 MPa would contradict the prediction without satisfying the falsification rule.

The hypothesis predicts retention of at least 90% of baseline ΔTad, but the experiment only falsifies it below 80%. Retention from 80% to below 90% would contradict the prediction without falsifying it under the stated rule.
